spaceobject.moon.desc:
A satellite of the Earth where helium-3 is mined and used to produce G-3 quantum fluid—fuel for cubecentric engines. The Moon has a sealed metropolis, New Seattle, which houses the headquarters and other buildings of a huge number of corporations. The Source complex deserves special mention, as it houses servers storing the current text of the NCE and other documents that could be described as the constitution of the AnCap system.

In a sense, New Seattle, a giant sparkling city beneath a dome covered with lunar soil to protect against radiation, is the heart of the AnCap system. According to the inhabitants of the Moon,Earth is a boring old planet. Whereas in the steel, plastic, and glass structures of New Seattle, life is in full swing, driven by the thirst for profit and the desire for freedom.
spaceobject.moon.name: Moon
spaceobject.moon.shortdesc:
The natural satellite of Earth, inhabited by people in colonies sheltered from radiation.
Main contributors to development: PlanetBridge, Grasshopper Tek.
Largest and only city: New Seattle.
spaceobject.pallas.desc:
A remote province of the Main Belt. Some consider living on Pallas to be hard and a major misfortune, while others, looking at events in the rest of the System, consider life here quiet and happy. However, with the onset of 2200, even the most remote corners of the System were affected by the new redistribution of property. Pallas is similar to a gray stone, both in terms of its exterior and in the feel of life here. People live a simple life, mining minerals and standing in huge lines after food transporters arrive.

At one time, Pallas was developed by the Hive corporation, and the asteroid essentially became its property. After the liquidation of the corporation, Pallas was of no use to anyone until platinum deposits were accidentally discovered under a small methane mine.
spaceobject.pallas.name: Pallas
spaceobject.pallas.shortdesc:
A large Main Belt asteroid, auxiliary stations and a mining facility.
Start of development: 2110s.
Main contributors to development: Hive.
spaceobject.phobos.desc:
Mars is a backwater relative to Earth. Phobos and Deimos are backwaters relative to Mars. Phobos is a natural satellite of Mars, a transfer station on the way to the Outer System. Its surface, dotted with craters and cracks, is home to transport hubs, warehouse systems, a mining factory and even the small colonyof Hypnos-2. This is a meeting place for many corporations and factions of the Outer System, whose agents cannot afford sufficient cover to infiltrate the Intercity.

Phobos is too cosmopolitan for the Inner System. And it’s not hard to find a recruiter for the piratesof the Unchained Belt or the Civil Resistance here.
spaceobject.phobos.name: Phobos
spaceobject.phobos.shortdesc:
A natural satellite of Mars, a transfer station on the way to the Outer System.
Start of development: 2050s.
Main contributors to development: RealWare, Grasshopper Tek.
Security status: not entirely safe.
spaceobject.phoebe.desc: Phoebe is a dark and grim irregular moon of <color=#FFFEC1>Saturn</color>. It travels on a retrograde orbit, making docking a matter of special maneuvering skill. Its surface is coated with carbonaceous ice and dust, making Phoebe one of the darkest moons in the Solar System. Believed to have been captured from the Kuiper Belt, it long remained on the periphery of corporate interest. Only with the development of long-range transport routes was it turned into a staging base for outer expeditions.
spaceobject.phoebe.name: Phoebe
spaceobject.phoebe.shortdesc:
Dark retrograde moon of Saturn.
Colonization began: 2160s.
Officially, only two staging bases are located here.
spaceobject.saturn.desc:
Saturn is a cold gas giant, around which its majestic rings gleam in pale light. Terraforming is impossible here, and development proceeds on two levels — the sparse shepherd stations orbiting Saturn itself, and construction on its moons and their orbits. The harvesters of helium-3 and hydrogen work in the upper atmosphere, while in the plane of the rings catcher stations collect icy asteroids for water, oxygen, and other gases. Cubecentric tugs haul the packaged ice to processing facilities, where it is converted into drinking water and fuel. The Saturn system is the water and gas reservoir of the entire Outer System and the future logistics hub for humanity’s continued expansion. Here the routes of Grasshopper Tek come to an end, here lie the last staging grounds of PlanetBridge, here Tianming places its most speculative investments, here Dilthey conducts fundamental observations of phenomena beyond the Solar System, and here SBN insurance is at its most expensive.

Saturn is humanity’s frontier; whoever holds the stations at Saturn stands guard over that frontier.
spaceobject.saturn.name: Saturn
spaceobject.saturn.shortdesc:
Gas giant. Colonization impossible.
Initial development: isolated efforts since the 2170s; colonization ongoing.
spaceobject.titan.desc:
Titan is the largest moon of Saturn and one of the most distinctive worlds of the Outer System. Its dense nitrogen-methane atmosphere paints the sky in murky yellow tones, concealing the surface beneath perpetual haze. Cold winds blow here, methane rains fall, and vast hydrocarbon seas stretch across the land. At present, it is possible to be on Titan without a hermetic spacesuit: a protective suit and a breathing filter are sufficient.

Titan has become the hub of hydrocarbon processing in the Outer System. Chemical complexes and refineries have been built here, supplying quantum liquid G-3 to stations on Saturn and its moons. Corporations compete for control of the logistics: whoever controls Titan controls the resources of the entire Outer System.
spaceobject.titan.name: Titan
spaceobject.titan.shortdesc:
Largest moon of Saturn.
Colonization began: 2140s.
Main contribution to the economy: fuel chemistry.
spaceobject.tsiolkovsky.desc:
A large artificial Earth satellite. Tsiolkovsky consists of a robust central structure (CS), an automatic orbit maintenance system, and five stations located in different parts of the CS. Tsiolkovsky was supposed to be a transport hub, a gateway to Earth. At the same time, it was supposed to be connected to the surface by a space elevator. So far, these plans have not been put into effect, since no corporation has the resources for such an ambitious project.

For a long time, it was not customary to initiate direct actions on Tsiolkovsky, as was the case in Earth’s orbit. But in the last decade and a half, hostilities have begun to occur at the Tsiolkovsky station. When they reach Earth is a matter of time.
spaceobject.tsiolkovsky.name: Tsiolkovsky
spaceobject.tsiolkovsky.shortdesc:
An artificial Earth satellite, a wonder of orbital engineering.
Created: 2120, the 20th anniversary of the GAR.
Creators: corporations of the Hexarchy.
spaceobject.venus.desc:
At the end of the 21st century, the full might of several corporations was directed at the intensive terraforming of the planet. The following were undertaken: bombardment with ice blocks, infection of the soil with GM bacteria, sowing of GM seeds, and then the settlement of GM animals (mainly insects and spiders). The terraforming process on Venus lasted 70 years, and people lost control of it at several stages. For example, the upper layers of the atmosphere became a toxic greenhouse under which jungles grew, and poisonous swamps still encircle the planet along the equator.

Despite all this, Venus is now the most habitable planet after Earth.
spaceobject.venus.name: Venus
spaceobject.venus.shortdesc:
Terraformed planet covered in GMO jungles.
Start of exploration: 2080s.
Major contributor to terraforming: Fresco.
spaceobject.vesta.desc:
Vesta constantly changes its status in trade and transport catalogues. One day it’s being called the largest asteroid in the System, the next it’s already laying claim to the title of the tiniest dwarf planet. However, these metamorphoses pale in comparison to the true value of Vesta— its endless mineral reserves, which attracted the attention of corporations to the asteroid almost immediately after the invention of the cubecentric engine. Now Vesta is cut through by kilometers of underground mines, many of which have long since been abandoned. Their tunnels plunge deep into its mineral heart.

Don’t be surprised if you are lucky enough to stumble upon a feral tribe of cannibals who have long forgotten that they live in space: in the dark abandoned labyrinths of the mines, time flows by its own laws. The people who are born, live and die here are no longer that similar to Earthlings.
spaceobject.vesta.name: Vesta
spaceobject.vesta.shortdesc:
A large Main Belt asteroid, a cluster of resource extraction facilities.
Start of development: 2100s.
Main contributors to development: CoreWard MG, Daydream Chem.
spaceobject.volcano.desc:
A steel and titanium monster that orbits high above Mercury. Its two halves, once independent spacecraft, are held together by a bulky, asymmetrical structure designed to withstand the unpredictable gravitational forces and solar winds. Vulcan houses three stations.

With its lead-gray hull and observation windows that gleam with the reflection of the Sun, Vulcan is reminiscent of the early years of active exploration of the Solar System. The noise of power reactors penetrates every corner, and the vibration of the hull is the soundtrack for the satellite's inhabitants.
spaceobject.volcano.name: Volcano
spaceobject.volcano.shortdesc:
An artificial satellite of Mercury, constructed from old spacecraft.
Altitude above Mercury: 120 Mm.
Year of creation: 2132.
Creators: Dilthey, PlanetBridge.
spaceobject.wernher.desc:
Wernher is a unique construction, built during the Great Anarchic Revolution (GAR) by the Dilthey corporation. An artificial planet, placed in the Main Belt in such a way as to move in orbit at a constant distance fromCeres. For about 40 years after its construction, Wernher was a Dilthey base, capable of moving throughout the System and taking part in the corporation's major construction projects: it participated in the capture and delivery of Geist to a new orbit, and was also a construction base for the construction of HAVOC buildings.

Wernher has now been placed in a permanent orbit in the Main Belt, and its cubecentric engines have gone dead forever. It contains three stations that have been converted into freely sold assets.
spaceobject.wernher.name: Wernher
spaceobject.wernher.shortdesc:
An artificial planet, the largest man-made object in the System.
Average distance to Sun: 2.8 AU
Year of creation: 2117.
Creator: Dilthey.
